title: Kkakdugi Radish Kimchi
shortDescription: Crunchy cubes of Korean radish are lightly salted, then coated with gochugaru, garlic, ginger, scallion, fish sauce, and salted shrimp for a bright, gradually souring kimchi.
culturalContext: Kkakdugi is a cubed-radish kimchi served across Korean home and restaurant tables, especially alongside soups. Radish size, sweetness, seasoning, and fermentation preference vary; this draft presents one common seafood-seasoned style.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Clean 2-liter glass or food-safe plastic container with headspace

ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into 2 cm / 3/4-inch cubes

instructions.heading: Prepare the radish
instructions.action: Wash, peel, and cut the radish into even 2 cm / 3/4-inch cubes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cubes are uniform enough to season and ferment at similar rates.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean board and wash produce under cool running water before cutting.

instructions.heading: Salt the cubes
instructions.action: Toss radish with salt and half the sugar. Rest 30 minutes, turning twice.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The radish glistens, releases some liquid, and remains crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the bowl protected from raw meat and seafood cross-contact.

instructions.heading: Drain
instructions.action: Drain the released liquid without rinsing. Let the cubes stand in a clean colander for 5 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The cubes are moist but no longer sitting in a pool of liquid.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a sanitized colander and sink area.

instructions.heading: Season
instructions.action: Wearing gloves, toss radish with gochugaru first, then add fish sauce, saeujeot, garlic, ginger, remaining sugar, and scallions.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every cube has an even red coating and seasoning collects lightly in the bowl.
instructions.safetyNote: Contains fish and shellfish; prevent seasoning from contacting ready-to-eat allergen-free foods.

instructions.heading: Pack
instructions.action: Press into a clean food-grade container, removing large air pockets and leaving at least 5 cm / 2 inches of headspace.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Radish is compactly packed and the rim is clean.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not fill to the lid because active fermentation can create gas and overflow.

instructions.heading: Ferment conservatively and chill
instructions.action: Refrigerate immediately for a fresh result, or hold in a cool room no more than 8 to 12 hours in this unreviewed draft, venting carefully, then refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C.
instructions.temperature: Cool room, then refrigerator at or below 40°F / 4°C
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Small bubbles and a clean tart aroma may develop while cubes stay crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard if mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration appears; final fermentation limits require qualified safety approval.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan does not use a grill.
visualDonenessCues: Radish cubes remain crisp after salting
Early fermentation may show small bubbles and a clean tart aroma
foodSafetyNotes: Use clean tools, gloves, containers, and potable water.
Keep seafood seasonings refrigerated according to their labels and disclose both fish and shellfish.
Leave headspace and vent sealed vessels carefully.
Refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C after the chosen short room-temperature stage.
Discard a batch with mold, putrid odor, or unusual discoloration.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish and crustacean shellfish; check all packaged seasonings for facility cross-contact.

substitutions: Daikon can replace Korean radish, but its higher moisture and softer texture require test-kitchen adjustment.
A vegan version needs a separately tested seasoning formula rather than simple omission of fish sauce and saeujeot.
ingredientSourcing: Choose a heavy, firm Korean radish with smooth skin and crisp white flesh.
Source gochugaru, Korean fish sauce, and saeujeot from a Korean market and check storage labels.
makeAhead: Cube and salt the radish only on assembly day; minced garlic and ginger may be prepared several hours ahead under refrigeration.
storage: Keep refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C in a clean container with headspace. Label the batch date; an approved shelf-life claim awaits fermentation-safety review.
reheating: Serve cold or cool; reheating is not recommended for this banchan.
leftovers: Use more-sour, otherwise sound kkakdugi in a thoroughly cooked dish only after the review team defines a validated storage window.
servingSuggestions: Spoon a small amount of radish and seasoning liquid into each dish

faq.question: Should kkakdugi stay crunchy?
faq.answer: Yes. Salting softens the surface slightly, but evenly cut radish should retain a crisp center.

faq.question: Can I refrigerate it immediately?
faq.answer: Yes. Immediate refrigeration gives a fresher profile and slower fermentation.
